questions.answer: A lot of information missing and a lot of confusing inbetween the host uni and the other uni and also just at the host university in regards of who to contact for certain questions and the courses.

questions.answer: Basically everything was cheaper than expected, especially taxi, beauty salons, tattoos, food and tickets to events (fx ballets). questions.answer: As many as possible.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Every attraction in the city.

Try out stuff like shooting bow and arrow, go to ballets and concerts.

Go outside the city: To Almaty, Karaganda, Turkmenistan (and other cities in south Kazakhstan)

Go to local and cultural restaurants.

Go out with friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, but the language berrier was difficult, but good so we could be better at it faster.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to approach people even tho it seems scary - use the opportunities you get. Attend events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The religion, the language. They are pretty religious and I'm not. But no problems.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were more friendly and welcoming and open than in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Experience everything you can, don't hold back. Of course you should study, but also prioritize having the best adventure of your life, don't make it an ordinary boring everyday life. Go to stuff, hang out with friends, make new friends, take trips, go sightseeing, meet locals.

Interact with the culture and really experience it - talk with locals and ask them questions, visit mosques fx to see how they live their culture, eat and drink local food and drinks (try everything), try out things that represents their culture.

Ask for help and reach out if needed. It can be your family, your friends, adult at the school, fellow students etc. It's a big and a bit scary exprerience in the beginning, but it's worth it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Ask fellow students who have been on exchange for help and advise.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To experience a lot of amazing things and really live a such a different culture, and getting amazing friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language berrier and making friends in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
